product.intro: FinBuddy tracks what came in, what went out, and what’s due for an INR household. Try the sample household to see a full month before starting your own.
sections: Set up a monthly check-in

Sign in with Google or email and start on Home. Record your salary and other money received under Income. Use the month selector to review the period you want. Home uses the records for that calendar month.
Log your first expense

Choose Add expense. Enter the amount and category, check the date, and save. Add a note, platform, person, or receipt when it helps. Open Expenses to find and edit an entry, or use it to review a past period.
Pay a bill without counting it twice

Open Bills & EMIs and add the amount and due date. When you pay, choose the matching expense if it is already in your ledger. You can also create the expense while recording the payment. This keeps the bill and the ledger connected.
See how spending fits your plan
Set a monthly amount for a category in Budgets. Open More, then Overview, to see category spending and the month’s highlights. Review the expense list before changing a budget based on the totals.
Update savings when values change

Open Savings and add a balance for an emergency fund, fixed deposit, SIP, or other holding. Add the date you checked it. Update the recorded value when it changes. Savings values come from your entries.
Troubleshooting

For sign-in, use the same provider you used to create your account. If a record seems missing, check your account, date range, and filters first. To investigate a bill total, open the bill and look for its linked expense. For old savings balances, check the date displayed beside the holding.

technical.intro: FinBuddy is a React and TypeScript web app built with Vite and served by Firebase Hosting.
sections: Account and storage

Firebase Authentication identifies the account. Cloud Firestore stores financial records and Cloud Storage holds receipt attachments. Security rules govern application access to those resources. Test account access and writes against Firebase emulators with fictional records.
Money and dates
FinBuddy stores amounts in integer paise and uses local calendar dates for monthly views. Bill payments can reference individual ledger entries. Savings hold recorded values with an as-of date.
REST API

Firebase Hosting routes /api/v1 to the separately deployed Firebase Functions API. Swagger lists operations for the supported resources, including expenses, budgets, bills, income and savings. Developer Options grants scoped tokens to the signed-in account.
Local development

Use Node.js 24 for the web app, Python 3.12 for public docs, and Java 21 for Firebase emulators. From the repository, run npm ci and npm run dev. Use the demo for inspection and the repository’s emulator commands to test data writes. The API codebase uses Node.js 22 in CI.
Public documentation

The product handbook and release pages are built from shared source. Firebase hosts the Help Center. GitHub Pages hosts the product site. Both builds validate internal links and publish a source revision.

settings.intro: In the signed-in app, open More → Settings. Settings opens to Preferences. Developer Options is a separate section in the Settings sidebar.
sections: Display mode
Light is the default. Choose Dark or System to follow your device’s light or dark preference. It takes effect immediately on this device.
Color palette

Lavender is the default. Choose another palette, including Black & white, under Color palette. It applies immediately to this device. Black & white sets the palette and works with your chosen display mode.
Font

Google Sans is the default. You can choose Source Sans 3, Source Code Pro, Lato, Open Sans, Ubuntu, Source Serif 4, Lora, or Roboto. Use Reset appearance to restore the display, palette, and font defaults on this device.
Token scope and expiration

In Developer Options, choose read-only for exports or read/write for integrations that change records. The default lifetime is 30 days. You can select 7 days, 90 days, or Never expires. Generating a token requires a recent sign-in, and the token is scoped to the account that created it.
Copy or revoke a token

Copy the token when it is displayed and save it in your integration’s secret store. In Swagger, use Authorize to test the scope. Revoke a token in Developer Options when an integration stops using it or you need to replace it.

sdlc.intro: FinBuddy follows the App Launchpad v1.14.0 solo-maintainer workflow. The GitHub Project records the work and the implementation PR records the release decision.
sections: Intake and planning
Give the issue an owner, type, and milestone. Describe the household outcome and how to verify it. Use dependencies to order scheduled work on the GitHub Project.
Development and documentation

Use a short-lived branch and link the implementation PR to the issue. Include the tests you ran and describe migration, rollout, and recovery where relevant. Record which guides changed or why the current guidance still applies.
Review and merge

Review the current candidate and resolve review threads. Foundation, web, and API checks must pass with the candidate up to date with main. The solo-maintainer policy requires zero independent approvals.
Release and recovery

Use synthetic fixtures in Firebase emulators and the approved preview channel if a hosted review is needed. A merge to main sends the tested web artifact to Hosting. Verify each deployed surface and use its documented recovery process if needed.

pipeline.intro: GitHub Actions checks each pull request. After merge, Firebase Hosting publishes the verified application artifact and GitHub Pages publishes the product site on changes that affect it.
sections: What CI verifies

Foundation checks project contracts, Markdown links, the PR documentation decision, and both public docs builds. The web job runs lint, unit tests, and browser scenarios with Firebase emulators. The API job runs unit and emulator tests with its own configuration.
When publication fails
Review the job for the affected host and verify the revision it serves. The release guide records when to retry a checked artifact, revert a documentation change, or restore a prior Hosting release.
stages: Check documentation impact, repository contracts, the web and API, and the public docs builds.
Re-run the web and API checks for the merge revision. The web build includes the Firebase Help Center and attaches the artifact used by Hosting.
Deploy the verified web artifact on Firebase Hosting. A separate packaging and publishing workflow deploys the GitHub Pages product site and guides.
Check the Hosting revision, assets, and API health. Open the changed guides, check links, and compare each guide’s source revision with the deployed commit.

roadmap.intro: See what households can use today and the checks that planned work must pass before wider access.
sections: Available now
The signed-in workspace supports income, expenses, budgets, bills and EMIs, and dated savings values. Anyone can tour the sample household without signing in.
FinVision integration · In discovery

The first slice aims to give signed-in FinBuddy users a place to see an agreed set of FinVision information. The current milestone covers planning and verification criteria. The implementation window follows agreement on identity, data ownership, and sync behavior.
KautilyaAI and Metrics Explorer · Coming soon
Both appear as Coming soon in the app. Their rollout windows are unscheduled. For current month-by-month spending insights, use Overview.
Replacement MCP integration · Backlog
Discovery will scope an agent connection, permitted actions, and account access. The intended audience is users who choose to connect an integration. This work has no scheduled rollout window.
stages: Map account identity and decide who owns each record before any cross-app sync.
First slice · After the contract is agreed
Plan the smallest FinVision page and specify the source of truth, sync direction, and conflict behavior.
Verify access boundaries, sync behavior, and recovery in emulators with fictional accounts before a limited release.
Review pilot evidence and approve the release scope. A public date follows those checks.

releases.intro: Browse FinBuddy by version. Each entry identifies whether its evidence comes from production, a source tag, or the changelog.
sections: How to read this history
A production entry links to deployment or release evidence. Source tags and changelog entries document earlier work and may describe features that have since changed.

Added editable expense templates, search, and default amounts.
Introduced app and platform categorisation for expenses.
